doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Jimmy Noon, Nene Quacku and the barbers
title: Musicians who were barbers; Chook, Yank Johnson and the Lundys
summary: Many musicians were barbers. Martin and Tom talk about Chook and the Lundy family, and about Yank Johnson following Tom's band around as a boy, learning horn on his gallery and playing for Louis. Yank was younger than Buddy.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: He's the same as Duck. All of them out there in Barber.
Seems like a lot of the musicians used to be barbers.
Do you remember any others? Was Buddy Johnson the barber? Yeah. That's what I thought.
That's where all them fellas, I can call them all almost. In my time on Tash Street, you take, you take, I used to play as you there, Chook. Chook, yeah.
Chook? Chook. Chook. That's what his name is, Chook. I don't know what his name is.
Chook. Chook. You take Lundy. You take Harrison Lundy, Bill Lundy, Boogerman Lundy, Yank didn't Lundy because Buddy wouldn't name him at home. He'd learn from Chook home, Yank. Oh yeah.
He did, yeah, because he used to follow us every Saturday night. Chook. I was playing in Gretna.

I was playing for Bucky. First they called Bucky. And then I'd leave there, I was playing for one o'clock and I'd leave there and I'd come over Frank and Louis Armstrong was playing. I've used to pass all the time, Yank playing in there.
Louis, Yank was playing for Louis.
Yank was playing for Louis. Well he used to follow me and Chook all the time. Used to carry Chook on with me. Everywhere we go, we call him Yank. He used to carry with it.

Yeah, you see his name was Oliver I believe. No. Oh, what that boy name is. Uh-uh. You remember when the, when the, when they had Paducah in them up there, Yank was learning playing horned in. When the, Sweevers would come here and played, uh. Played ball. Played. Car Lake and them up there. You know. Yank was playing. Playing horned in. On that horned in.

Well I know, I know because, I know but Yank playing cause he followed us from, everywhere we went playing Yank was with it. Yeah. Yeah. Came Chook on. Yeah, yeah. And after, after he got so great he beat Chook. Chook died afterwards. Yeah. Yeah, well we took, and I took Yank and played. Yeah. I played with it for you, Yank. Was Yank older or younger than Buddy? No, he was younger than Buddy. Younger than Buddy. Younger than Buddy.
Yank was younger. Yank was older than me. Yeah. Yank was older than me.

Yank was older than me. Yank was a, Yank was playing ball with them people then cause the baseball team was, uh, game, uh, field was right in front of his house. Yeah, yeah. Yank used to sit up there while we'd be out there playing ball, uh, kids playing ball. Yank would be on that gallery with that horn. Not small.
